question: Why are time and desire not ultimately real causes in the universal sequence?
premises: Time and desire are presented as two causes in the universal sequence.
These two causes are explicitly negated as essentially real.
Their causal status is thus denied at the ultimate level.
inference: Time and desire function as causes only conventionally, not as ultimately real principles.
plain_english: Thus, in the universal sequence, the two causes, time and desire, are not ultimately real in essence.
